clue.text: Not so old housing collapsed after year

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters behind the abbreviation for year
something collapsed has fallen into disorder, so the letters of housing are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building that has fallen down not long after it was put up, so it is still fairly new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like a building, but it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means somewhat, so a person somewhat young is not so old as others.

clue.text: Some men use these tips for titillation

indicators.note: the tips of words are their opening letters here, taken from the four words at the start of the clue

explanation.surface: Some men apparently rely on these pieces of advice to arouse interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice, but it means the first letters of 'Some men use these'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent material whose purpose is sexual titillation, so the one stands for the other.

clue.text: Working stiff from Haiti

parts.note: a working stiff is an ordinary labourer, but read literally it is a corpse that works, the walking dead of Haitian vodou folklore

explanation.surface: A description of an ordinary labourer from Haiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working stiff' is slang for a humble worker; here 'stiff' is a corpse that has been set to work.
explanation.definitionFit: In Haitian folklore a corpse is revived by sorcery to labour as a mindless servant: a reanimated stiff that works.

clue.text: Start playing in attack when winning

parts.note: to strike is to attack
a team that is ahead is up, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A footballer comes into the side in attack while the team is ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A band strikes up a tune when it begins to perform music.

clue.text: Terrible tickle in chest — do this before you die!

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters within the word for chest

parts.note: bust means the chest or bosom

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of tickle are in a bad state and must be reworked

explanation.surface: A dreadful tickly feeling in one's chest, offered as something to experience before dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' signals the anagram and 'in' the container; the definition is a cheeky instruction rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish list of experiences to complete before death, from the idiom about kicking the pail.

clue.text: Eye damage from sun, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a bruised, blackened eye from a punch
the sun is an example of something that gives off light, so it is a thing that beams

explanation.surface: Damage to the eye caused by staring at the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a black eye, and literally anything that gives off light, like the sun.

clue.text: Report on economic success indicates it's a joke!

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a boom
a boom is a period of rapid economic growth

explanation.surface: A news report about a thriving economy is so rosy it must be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation was the catchphrase of the British puppet fox Basil Brush, said after each of his gags.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is the comedian's drum-sting punchline, said to signal that a gag has just landed.

clue.text: They like being with people and often lift spirits

definitions.meaning: sociable people who mingle easily at gatherings
soft drinks such as tonic or soda added to gin or whisky

explanation.surface: Description of cheerful folk who enjoy company and raise others' mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociable types who mingle at parties, and the tonics and sodas that dilute alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: You got me to put note around that hurt

indicators.note: the note is put around, so its two letters enclose the cry of pain

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
ouch is what you say when something has hurt you

explanation.surface: Someone concedes defeat and asks another to write a note about the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator 'put ... around' is split by its object; 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing term for an acknowledged hit, used in conversation to concede a good point.

clue.text: Spoon out extreme bits found in nasal cavity

indicators.note: the extreme bits of words are their first and last letters, here of the first two words

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to scoop things out from inside the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extreme bits' takes S and N from 'Spoon' and O and T from 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal mucus, a slang word for the stuff lodged in the nostrils.

clue.text: Routine bureaucratic approach with a potentially explosive package?

definitions.meaning: mechanical compliance with forms and checklists, marking each square without thought
a carton with a timer clicking inside it, which might be a bomb

explanation.surface: Officials process a suspicious parcel by rote, filling in forms.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase is a box that is ticking, like a bomb with a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindless form-filling is a box-checking exercise; a container that ticks may hold a timed bomb.

clue.text: Serbians detest commerce? At heart, I don't care

indicators.note: the heart of each word is its middle, here the central two letters of the three words before

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Serbs hate trade and then shrugs off the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At heart' takes BI from Serbians, TE from detest, and ME from commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude slangy retort expressing contempt or indifference to what another person says.

clue.text: Auntie has a concoction that puts one to sleep

definitions.note: a noun-like phrase: something that puts a person to sleep for good

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An aunt has brewed a drink that sends you to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' shuffles AUNTIE HAS, with the final A added beside it; 'puts one to sleep' is a euphemism for killing painlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercy killing; to put an animal or person to sleep is the euphemism for ending life painlessly.

clue.text: Again catalogues begrudgers rejecting society

indicators.note: rejecting means the society letter is thrown out of the word for begrudgers

parts.note: people who resent something are resenters

explanation.surface: Grumblers keep turning up in catalogues even though society rejects them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' drops one S from RESENTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to record in a list or register, so doing it a second time fits.

clue.text: Poet and wife killer

parts.note: a hitman is a hired killer

explanation.surface: A poet and a wife who murders, perhaps in a crime story.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt of that surname was the American author of Leaves of Grass.

clue.text: West's leader becoming a calamity?

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, of the word for the West changes into the letter a

parts.note: the Occident is the West
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Western leader turning out to be a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader becoming a' swaps the O of OCCIDENT for A. The question mark admits not every mishap is a calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap or unfortunate event, which at worst can be a disaster.

clue.text: Elastic band stuck in clock

indicators.note: stuck in places the band within the word for clock

parts.note: to clock is slang for to notice or spot, as is spy
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: An elastic band jammed in a clock's works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' is a verb here, slang for notice; 'stuck in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with bounce that returns to shape after stretching, like a coil of wire.

clue.text: Complaining about president is exciting

indicators.note: about means going round, so the complaining word goes around the president letter

parts.note: griping means complaining

explanation.surface: Moaning about the president is thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrilling story holds the attention firmly, as if seizing hold of the reader.

clue.text: Being careless is responsible for United getting relegated

indicators.note: relegated means moved down, so the United letter drops lower in the word

parts.note: causal means being the cause of, responsible for
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A football commentator blaming sloppiness for United's relegation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting relegated' moves the U of CAUSAL further down, after the S. In a down clue that is literally lower.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand, relaxed or careless attitude, showing little concern.

clue.text: Foreign office accountant caught spies forging Italian product

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, Britain's foreign ministry
CA is a chartered accountant
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: A diplomatic scandal in which officials and spies forge Italian goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forging' looks like a crime but simply links the pieces to what they make.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat Italian bread made with olive oil, an Italian bakery item.

clue.text: Compensation for travelling group

parts.note: to be off is to be leaving or on the way
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Payment owed to a touring party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that balances or counteracts another thing, as a carbon credit balances emissions.

clue.text: Nothing is shown by glib sort of language

indicators.note: shown by puts the glib word first, before the nothing and is

parts.note: pat means glib, too ready and slick
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slick speaker's way of talking reveals nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional dialect or non-standard form of speech, a variety of a tongue.

clue.text: Toilet break after surgery

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot, a toilet
a stop is a break or pause

explanation.surface: A trip to the lavatory needed once an operation is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for postoperative, describing the period following an operation.

clue.text: Faust's bind is desperate, with many reservations

indicators.note: desperate means in a wild, frantic state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Faust, bound by his pact with the devil, is desperate and full of doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' shuffles FAUSTS BIND.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for qualifications, objections and excuses raised against a plan.

clue.text: Record overseas resident returning when vote is lost

indicators.note: is lost means the voting mark drops out
returning means the word for the overseas resident is read backwards

parts.note: an expat is someone living abroad
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: An expatriate coming home has lost their vote and wants it on record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses EXPAT to TAPXE; 'is lost' removes X.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something is to capture it on magnetic media, as with a cassette.

clue.text: Trouser part of Greek attire is raised

indicators.note: is raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A trouser leg forming part of an outfit worn in Greece is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Trouser part' as the definition, but 'part of' is what signals the hidden letters, so the definition is 'Trouser', a verb. 'is raised' reads them upward, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser is British slang for pocketing money, often dishonestly, so it means to take.

clue.text: Army prisoner restraint is missing lower end

indicators.note: is missing means the chosen letter is taken away

parts.note: a leg iron is a shackle for a prisoner

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of lower

explanation.surface: An army's prisoner has slipped the bottom part of his shackles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower end' is the R that ends lower, which 'is missing' takes out of LEG IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army unit, and the word means a large body of soldiers.

clue.text: Putting together orchestral opening as interlude for musical

indicators.note: an interlude comes in the middle, so the letter goes inside the word for putting together

parts.note: linking means joining, putting together

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of orchestral

explanation.surface: Assembling a musical with an orchestral overture and a break in between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as interlude' puts O, the opening of orchestral, inside LINKING.
explanation.definitionFit: A Disney stage show adapted from the film about Simba, the young lion of Pride Rock.
